Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with language model generation.
Instead of relying solely on the model's parametric knowledge, RAG fetches relevant documents from an external corpus and uses them as context.
This approach reduces hallucinations and allows the model to answer questions about documents it was never trained on.
The retrieval step typically uses embedding-based semantic search, keyword search like BM25, or a hybrid of both.
Cross-encoder rerankers then reorder the retrieved results for better precision before passing them to the language model.
